title: HOSA Nutrition: Vitamins and Minerals - Nutrition - Vitamins
subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following vitamins is classified as **fat-soluble**, meaning it requires dietary fat for absorption and is stored in the body's liver and fatty tissues?
questions.explain: Vitamins are classified by solubility. Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble and stored in the body, whereas B-complex vitamins and Vitamin C are water-soluble.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient presents with **night blindness** and dry, scaly skin. A deficiency in which of the following vitamins is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: Vitamin A is essential for the formation of rhodopsin, a pigment in the retina responsible for vision in low light. Deficiency leads to nyctalopia (night blindness) and xerophthalmia.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesized in the skin upon exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation from sunlight?
questions.explain: Vitamin D (cholecalciferol) is synthesized in the skin when 7-dehydrocholesterol reacts with UVB light.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with bowed legs and skeletal deformities. This condition, known as **Rickets**, is caused by a deficiency in:
questions.explain: Rickets is a childhood condition caused by Vitamin D, calcium, or phosphate deficiency, leading to soft and weak bones.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which vitamin is known chemically as **ascorbic acid** and is essential for collagen synthesis?
questions.explain: Vitamin C is also known as ascorbic acid. It is a cofactor for enzymes that hydroxylate proline and lysine in collagen synthesis.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Gingivitis, petechiae (small blood spots), and delayed wound healing are classic signs of **Scurvy**. This results from a severe lack of:
questions.explain: Scurvy is the clinical manifestation of severe Vitamin C deficiency, leading to the breakdown of collagen-rich tissues.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient on long-term antibiotic therapy may develop a deficiency in this vitamin because it is partially synthesized by intestinal bacteria. Its primary role is in blood clotting.
questions.explain: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X. It is produced by gut flora, which can be disrupted by antibiotics.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which B-vitamin is correctly matched with its chemical name?
questions.explain: The correct pairings are: B1 (Thiamine), B2 (Riboflavin), B3 (Niacin), and B12 (Cobalamin).
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A deficiency in **Thiamine (Vitamin B1)** is associated with which condition, characterized by nerve damage and muscle wasting?
questions.explain: Beriberi is caused by thiamine deficiency. 'Dry' beriberi affects the nervous system, while 'wet' beriberi affects the cardiovascular system.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which nutrient is critical for women of childbearing age to prevent **neural tube defects** (like spina bifida) in the developing fetus?
questions.explain: Adequate Folate intake before and during early pregnancy is crucial for proper closure of the neural tube.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Strict vegans are most at risk for developing a deficiency in which vitamin, as it is found naturally only in animal products?
questions.explain: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) is found almost exclusively in animal foods. Vegans typically require supplementation or fortified foods.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: The deficiency disease **Pellagra** is characterized by the "4 Ds": Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia, and Death. It is caused by a lack of:
questions.explain: Pellagra is a systemic disease resulting from a deficiency in Niacin (Vitamin B3).
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: **Pernicious anemia** is a specific type of anemia caused by the body's inability to absorb Vitamin B12 due to a lack of:
questions.explain: Intrinsic factor, a protein secreted by the stomach, is required for Vitamin B12 absorption in the ileum. Pernicious anemia is an autoimmune attack on parietal cells that produce intrinsic factor.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Excessive intake of this fat-soluble vitamin is teratogenic (causes birth defects) and can lead to liver toxicity.
questions.explain: Vitamin A (specifically preformed retinoids) can be toxic in high doses, causing birth defects and liver damage. Beta-carotene (precursor) is generally safer.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which vitamin functions primarily as an antioxidant, protecting cell membranes from oxidative damage?
questions.explain: Vitamin E (tocopherol) is a major lipid-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes (polyunsaturated fatty acids) from oxidation.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Cheilosis (cracks at the corners of the mouth) and glossitis (inflamed tongue) are classic signs of a deficiency in:
questions.explain: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency (ariboflavinosis) manifests as lesions on the lips (cheilosis), mouth angles (stomatitis), and tongue (glossitis).
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Biotin (Vitamin B7) deficiency is rare but can be induced by the excessive consumption of raw:
questions.explain: Raw egg whites contain avidin, a protein that binds strongly to biotin and prevents its absorption. Cooking denatures avidin.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Hemolytic anemia in premature infants can be caused by a deficiency in this vitamin, which protects red blood cell membranes.
questions.explain: Premature infants have low Vitamin E stores. Deficiency makes red blood cell membranes susceptible to oxidative hemolysis.
questions.subject: Nutrition
